The handler then dereferences that NULL attribute slot — passing it to nla_parse_nested_deprecated / nla_data / nla_len — causing a NULL-pointer dereference and kernel oops (local DoS; potentially worse if a missing value feeds a length/bounds computation). Transferable invariant: in netlink-backed command handlers, the attribute-presence validation must prove every attribute that is later dereferenced is non-NULL; a guard that is logically inverted, checks a different attribute than the one used, is absent entirely, or relies on a policy that does not mark the attribute required/nested-validated, leaves a NULL-or-unchecked attributes[] slot that is later treated as a valid pointer. Attacker-controlled source: userspace-supplied netlink message attribute set (presence/absence and payloads fully attacker-chosen). Missing guarantee: per-attribute non-NULL (required) validation before use. Unsafe use: dereference or nested-parse of an attributes[]/tb[] slot without a covering check. Consequence: NULL-deref oops from unprivileged input, or OOB access when the unchecked value drives sizes/indices.
